title: Technical Sales and Service Coordinator
description:
SF Partners are supporting an established Shrewsbury SW1 based business that are looking to recruit a Technical Sales and Service Coordinator on a permanent basis.

Salary: £35,000-£45,000
Working pattern: full time site based

We are seeking an experienced Technical Sales and Service Co-Ordinator to provide professional support to customers and internal departments throughout the sales and service process. The successful candidate will have previous experience in a similar role, the ability to interpret technical drawings, and a proven track record of providing technical advice, coordinating appointments, resolving customer issues, and arranging collections and deliveries. Proficiency in SAP is essential.
Key Responsibilities
- Respond promptly and professionally to customer enquiries, providing accurate technical and product information.
- Read, interpret and apply technical drawings, specifications and associated documentation.
- Advise customers on appropriate products, services and technical solutions in accordance with their requirements.
- Prepare, process and follow up quotations, orders and service-related documentation.
- Arrange and co-ordinate customer appointments, site visits, installations, inspections and service callouts.
- Arrange the collection and delivery of products, equipment and materials in liaison with customers, drivers, suppliers and relevant internal departments.
- Monitor orders and service requests, providing customers with timely updates regarding progress, delivery schedules and any changes.
- Investigate and resolve customer queries and service issues efficiently, escalating complex matters where appropriate.
- Maintain accurate customer, order, delivery and service records within SAP and other relevant business systems.
- Work collaboratively with the sales, service, warehouse, transport and technical teams to ensure the efficient operation of day-to-day activities.
- Provide support with stock management, returns, warranty claims and after-sales service processes as required.
- Ensure that all activities are conducted in accordance with company procedures, regulatory requirements and established customer service

Desirable Experience
- Experience within an engineering, manufacturing, construction, industrial or other technical environment.
- Experience coordinating deliveries, collections, installations or field-service activities.
- Familiarity with quotations, purchase orders, sales orders, returns and warranty processes.
- A relevant technical qualification or industry-specific training.

title: Purchasing Administrator
description:
Purchasing Administrator

£28 - £32,000 per annum

Permanent

Telford

Overview
As a Purchasing Administrator, you will support purchasing activity by maintaining accurate order information and coordinating updates across purchasing, supply chain and logistics processes. You will work with colleagues and suppliers to help keep purchasing records clear and orders moving smoothly.

Purchasing and Procurement Administration
- Raise and process purchase orders in accordance with company procedures.
- Ensure purchase orders are accurate, authorised and issued to suppliers in a timely manner.
- Obtain and compare supplier quotations to support purchasing decisions.
- Liaise with suppliers regarding pricing, availability, lead times and delivery schedules.
- Monitor outstanding purchase orders and proactively chase suppliers for updates.
- Ensure orders are placed in line with agreed stock requirements, production schedules and purchasing budgets.
- Maintain accurate purchasing records and supplier documentation.
- Support the purchasing team with general administrative duties and procurement activities.

Production and Materials Support
- Work closely with the Production, Planning, Stores and Warehouse teams to understand material and component requirements.
- Monitor material availability and identify potential shortages that could impact production.
- Help ensure materials and components are ordered in line with manufacturing schedules.
- Communicate expected delivery dates and potential delays to relevant departments.
- Assist in resolving supply issues to minimise disruption to production.
- Support stock replenishment activities and help maintain appropriate stock levels.
- Highlight obsolete, excess or slow-moving stock where identified.

title: First Point of Contact Administrator
description:
First Point of Contact Administrator

Location: Shrewsbury
Salary: £25,500 per annum increasing to £26,600 after probation
Job Type: Full Time
Training & Support: Full training provided

We are currently recruiting for a First Point of Contact Administrator to join a busy property management team based in Shrewsbury.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone with strong customer service, administration and communication skills who is looking to develop their career within the property sector. Full training and ongoing support will be provided.

As the first point of contact, you will play an important role in providing a professional and efficient service to clients, customers, contractors and leaseholders.

You will be responsible for handling incoming calls and emails, dealing with routine enquiries and ensuring more complex queries are directed to the appropriate Property Manager or department.

Key Responsibilities
- Answer incoming telephone calls and emails, providing a professional and helpful first point of contact.
- Handle routine client and customer enquiries and accurately triage more complex queries.
- Direct calls and correspondence to the appropriate Property Manager or internal department.
- Prepare and issue general correspondence to clients and leaseholders.
- Assist Property Managers and Department Heads with client, contractor and customer communications.
- Upload and maintain documentation across internal systems.
- Manage appointments and oversee the Shrewsbury office diary.
- Liaise with internal teams to obtain and provide information relating to property portfolios.
- Attend internal meetings where required.
- Ensure all work is carried out in line with relevant industry guidelines and best practice.
- Complete mandatory training and participate in additional training where appropriate.
- Maintain high standards of customer service and ensure customers are treated fairly.
- Keep up to date with relevant legislation and industry developments.
- Work collaboratively as part of a wider property management team.

About You

We are looking for someone who is:
- Customer-focused with a professional and friendly approach.
- Confident communicating by telephone, email and in person.
- Highly organised with good attention to detail.
- Comfortable managing multiple enquiries and prioritising workload.
- IT literate and confident using internal systems.
- A strong team player who is willing to learn and develop.
- Reliable, punctual and professional.
- Previous experience in administration, customer service, property or a similar environment would be beneficial, although not essential.

What's on Offer?
- £25,500 per annum increasing to £26,600 after probation
- Full training and ongoing support
- Opportunity to develop a career within the property management sector
- Supportive team environment
- Excellent opportunity for someone looking to establish themselves within residential property

If you're organised, personable and looking for an opportunity to build your career within property, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Office Administrator
description:
Job Title: Office Executive
Location: Telford, UK

Employment Type: Full-Time

Office Operations

Manage the day-to-day functioning of the office, including workspace allocation, meeting rooms, and reception services.

Ensure office upkeep, maintenance coordination, and effective space utilization.

Maintain a safe, efficient, and professional work environment.

Vendor Management

Manage and coordinate external vendors, including security, housekeeping, maintenance, and catering providers.

Monitor vendor performance against agreed SLAs and drive continuous service improvements.

Ensure timely resolution of operational and service-related issues.

Cost Management

Monitor operational budgets, invoices, and overall expenditure.

Identify and implement cost-saving initiatives while maintaining service quality.

Ensure effective budget utilization and financial discipline across office operations.

Health, Safety & Compliance

Ensure compliance with workplace health, safety, and regulatory standards.

Support internal and external audits, risk assessments, and safety drills.

Maintain compliance documentation and records as required.

Employee Experience

Deliver a high-quality workplace and visitor experience.

Manage office services, including pantry operations, office supplies, amenities, and event support.

Address employee concerns related to workplace facilities and services.

Administration & Governance

Oversee courier services, logistics, and general administrative activities.

Maintain operational records, MIS reports, and compliance documentation.

Ensure adherence to organizational policies and procedures.

Stakeholder Coordination

Collaborate closely with HR, IT, Finance, and business teams to support operational requirements.

Act as the primary escalation point for office-related issues.

Foster strong relationships with internal and external stakeholders.

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

Smooth and uninterrupted office operations.

Vendor SLA compliance of 95% or above.

Achievement of cost-saving initiatives and budget adherence.

Enhanced employee and visitor satisfaction.

Compliance with health, safety, and audit standards.

Qualifications & Experience

3-5 years of relevant experience in Office Management, Facilities Management, or Administration.

Experience working in a corporate office environment.

Proven experience in vendor management, administration, and cost tracking.

Working knowledge of workplace health, safety, and compliance practices.

Skills & Competencies

Resourceful, self-motivated, and proactive approach.

Strong focus on cost efficiency and value creation.

Ability to work independently with a high sense of ownership.

Hands-on execution and problem-solving skills.

Excellent vendor management and stakeholder engagement abilities.

Strong communication and organizational skills.

Behavioral Expectations

Takes initiative and proactively goes beyond assigned responsibilities.

Continuously identifies opportunities for operational improvements and cost savings.

Demonstrates accountability, ownership, and a results-oriented mindset.

Delivers outcomes with speed, quality, and professionalism.

Seymour John are supporting a well-established business in Oswestry, who are looking for an experienced Accounts Assistant to join their finance team on an 11-month fixed-term contract.

This is a hands-on role covering both sides of the ledger, including invoice processing, reconciliations, payments, cash books and month-end support. You will be joining a busy finance office where accuracy, organisation and the ability to meet deadlines are essential.

- Processing purchase invoices, including raw material and sundry invoices

- Reconciling the finance system against the transactional system
- Updating and reconciling cash books and processing customer direct debits
- Completing Sales Ledger month-end processes and reconciliations
- Supporting audits and providing general cover across the finance office

We are looking for someone with previous experience working in a similar role. You should be comfortable handling a varied transactional workload and have practical experience across Purchase Ledger, Sales Ledger or both.

Experience within a manufacturing environment would be useful but is not essential. You will need strong attention to detail, good Excel skills, and the ability to organise your workload effectively while working to deadlines.

- Cycle 2 Work scheme

- Enhanced Maternity/Paternity pay
- Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

The Company

A successful and growing technology-led manufacturing business that designs and supplies specialist products and solutions to a diverse range of industry sectors. Known for its focus on innovation, quality and customer service, the company offers a collaborative working environment and continues to invest in new technologies, people and processes to support its ongoing growth.

The Role

We are seeking an organised and proactive Accounts Assistant to manage customer invoicing, payment allocation, credit control and account reconciliations. Working closely with the Finance team and wider business, you'll help maintain accurate financial records, support cash flow management and contribute to the company's overall financial performance.

The ideal candidate will be hands-on, detail-focused and able to manage priorities effectively while maintaining a high level of accuracy.

Accounts Receivable & Credit Control
- Manage the day-to-day sales ledger, ensuring invoices are raised accurately and on time.
- Allocate customer payments, maintain account records and set up new customer accounts.
- Investigate and resolve invoice, payment and account queries.
- Monitor outstanding balances and proactively chase overdue payments.
- Build strong customer relationships to support prompt payment and minimise aged debt.
- Produce aged debtor reports and escalate payment concerns where required.

Reporting & Reconciliations
- Perform regular customer account and sales ledger reconciliations.
- Support month-end and year-end reporting activities.
- Assist with audits and ensure transactions are recorded in line with company procedures and accounting standards.

Finance Team Support
- Support the wider Finance team, including Accounts Payable when required.
- Work closely with internal departments to ensure accurate invoicing and resolve account queries.
- Contribute to process improvements, system enhancements and ad hoc finance projects.

Knowledge, Skills & Experience
- Previous experience in Accounts Receivable, Credit Control or a similar finance role.
- Strong understanding of sales ledger processes, reconciliations and financial controls.
- Confident using finance systems (ideally Xero) and Microsoft Excel.
- Excellent attention to detail, numerical accuracy and problem-solving skills.
- Strong communication skills with the ability to build positive relationships with customers and colleagues.
- Proactive, organised and able to work independently as well as part of a team.
- Experience within a manufacturing, engineering or technical environment preferred.
- Exposure to month-end processes, financial reporting and process improvements would be beneficial.
- Experience of international customers, foreign currency transactions or US Sales Tax is advantageous but not essential.

title: Finance Assistant
description:
ob Title: Finance Assistant

Location: Wellington, Somerset

Salary: 29,000m - 33,000 PA DOE

Hours: 30 - 35 hours per week, Monday to Friday

Flexible for the candidate

Benefit Package:
- 25 days holiday plus bank holidays
- Company pension scheme
- Annual Company Bonus based on performance
- Cycle 2 Work scheme
- Up to 2 days per year for volunteering
- Enhanced Maternity/Paternity pay
- Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
- Death in service insurance (4 x salary after probation)

The Company

A successful and growing technology-led manufacturing business that designs and supplies specialist products and solutions to a diverse range of industry sectors. Known for its focus on innovation, quality and customer service, the company offers a collaborative working environment and continues to invest in new technologies, people and processes to support its ongoing growth.

The Role

We are seeking an organised and proactive Accounts Assistant to manage customer invoicing, payment allocation, credit control and account reconciliations. Working closely with the Finance team and wider business, you'll help maintain accurate financial records, support cash flow management and contribute to the company's overall financial performance.

The ideal candidate will be hands-on, detail-focused and able to manage priorities effectively while maintaining a high level of accuracy.

Key Responsibilities

Accounts Receivable & Credit Control
- Manage the day-to-day sales ledger, ensuring invoices are raised accurately and on time.
- Allocate customer payments, maintain account records and set up new customer accounts.
- Investigate and resolve invoice, payment and account queries.
- Monitor outstanding balances and proactively chase overdue payments.
- Build strong customer relationships to support prompt payment and minimise aged debt.
- Produce aged debtor reports and escalate payment concerns where required.

Reporting & Reconciliations
- Perform regular customer account and sales ledger reconciliations.
- Support month-end and year-end reporting activities.
- Assist with audits and ensure transactions are recorded in line with company procedures and accounting standards.

Finance Team Support
- Support the wider Finance team, including Accounts Payable when required.
- Work closely with internal departments to ensure accurate invoicing and resolve account queries.
- Contribute to process improvements, system enhancements and ad hoc finance projects.

Knowledge, Skills & Experience
- Previous experience in Accounts Receivable, Credit Control or a similar finance role.
- Strong understanding of sales ledger processes, reconciliations and financial controls.
- Confident using finance systems (ideally Xero) and Microsoft Excel.
- Excellent attention to detail, numerical accuracy and problem-solving skills.
- Strong communication skills with the ability to build positive relationships with customers and colleagues.
- Proactive, organised and able to work independently as well as part of a team.
- Experience within a manufacturing, engineering or technical environment preferred.
- Exposure to month-end processes, financial reporting and process improvements would be beneficial.

Next Steps:

To apply, please do so online or email your CV to (url removed). If you would like to discuss the role in more detail prior to application please call Vicky on (phone number removed).

title: Stock Control & Purchasing Coordinator
description:
Supply Chain Development within a Leading Equipment Supplier
Location - Shrewsbury
Salary: up to 40,000 pa + Benefits
Are you an experienced Stock Control or Purchasing professional looking for a varied role where you can take ownership of inventory management, purchasing and supplier relationships?
We are working with an established business looking to appoint a proactive and organised Stock Control & Purchasing Coordinator to support its operational requirements and ensure the efficient availability of materials, products and equipment.
The Role
You will play an important part in managing stock levels and coordinating purchasing activities, ensuring materials are available when needed while maintaining accurate records and controlling inventory costs.
Key responsibilities will include:
- Monitoring stock levels and raising purchase orders to meet operational requirements.
- Managing the purchasing process from obtaining supplier quotations through to order placement and delivery.
- Using SAP to maintain accurate inventory records, process purchase orders and manage goods receipts.
- Liaising with suppliers to track deliveries, resolve shortages and investigate stock discrepancies.
- Maintaining appropriate inventory levels while minimising excess, obsolete and slow-moving stock.
- Coordinating the supply of materials, equipment and consumables to support day-to-day operations.
- Monitoring supplier performance, pricing and lead times, identifying opportunities for improved efficiency and cost control.
- Producing stock, purchasing and supplier reports using SAP, Excel and other IT systems.
- Working closely with warehouse, finance and operational teams to ensure purchasing and stock control processes run smoothly.

About You

We're keen to speak with individuals who have previous experience in stock control, purchasing, procurement, materials management or supply chain coordination.
You'll ideally bring:
- Practical experience using SAP or a similar ERP system within a purchasing or inventory environment - essential.
- Strong Microsoft Office and Excel skills.
- Excellent organisational skills and attention to detail.
- The ability to manage competing priorities and work to deadlines.
- Good communication and supplier relationship management skills.
- A proactive, methodical and solutions-focused approach to resolving supply and stock issues.

Experience within a manufacturing, engineering, warehouse or wider operational environment would be particularly advantageous.
Interested?
This is an excellent opportunity to join an established operation in a varied position combining purchasing, stock management and supplier coordination. If this sounds like the right next step in your career, we would love to hear from you. Please apply with your full CV, quoting reference number 10576.

title: SAP Stock Control & Purchasing Coordinator
description:
The Opportunity

We are recruiting for an organised and proactive Stock Control & Purchasing Coordinator to join an established organisation.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone with experience in purchasing, stock control and inventory management who enjoys working in a hands-on, operational environment.

The successful candidate will be responsible for maintaining accurate stock records, coordinating purchasing activities, managing supplier deliveries and ensuring materials, products and equipment are available when required.

You will use SAP and Microsoft Excel to support inventory accuracy, purchasing efficiency and operational performance.

Key Responsibilities Stock Control & Inventory Management
- Monitor stock levels and ensure materials and products are available to meet operational requirements.
- Maintain accurate inventory records using SAP and other relevant systems.
- Investigate stock discrepancies, shortages and delivery issues.
- Conduct regular stock checks and support periodic stocktakes.
- Monitor excess, obsolete and slow-moving stock, identifying opportunities to improve inventory efficiency.
- Ensure stock movements and goods receipts are recorded accurately.

Purchasing & Supplier Coordination
- Raise and process purchase orders in line with business requirements.
- Obtain supplier quotations and support purchasing decisions.
- Monitor outstanding orders and follow up with suppliers to ensure timely delivery.
- Review supplier pricing, lead times and delivery performance.
- Resolve purchasing and delivery discrepancies, escalating issues where necessary.
- Maintain accurate supplier and purchasing records.

Administration & Reporting
- Prepare purchasing, stock and supplier performance reports using SAP and Excel.
- Monitor inventory information to identify potential supply issues.
- Work closely with Finance, Warehouse and Operations teams to resolve discrepancies.
- Ensure purchasing documentation, goods receipts and stock records are accurate and up to date.
- Support improvements to purchasing and stock control procedures.
- Follow relevant health and safety, quality and operational procedures.

Essential Skills & Experience
- Previous experience in stock control, purchasing, procurement administration, supply chain or materials coordination.
- Practical, hands-on experience using SAP for purchasing, inventory management or goods receipting.
- Experience raising purchase orders, managing suppliers and tracking deliveries.
- Good understanding of stock accuracy, inventory levels and stocktaking procedures.
- Confident using Microsoft Excel and other IT systems.
- Strong organisational skills and excellent attention to detail.
- Ability to investigate stock discrepancies and resolve issues effectively.
- Good communication skills when dealing with suppliers and internal stakeholders.
- Ability to work independently and manage competing priorities.

Desirable Experience
- Previous experience within manufacturing, engineering, warehousing, facilities or industrial operations.
- Knowledge of inventory forecasting, replenishment and stock rotation.
- Experience producing purchasing and inventory reports.
- Understanding of supplier management, pricing and cost-control principles.
- Experience improving stock accuracy and purchasing processes.

The Ideal Candidate

We are looking for someone who is organised, reliable, proactive and confident working with purchasing and stock management systems.

You will be comfortable managing purchase orders, investigating stock issues, communicating with suppliers and ensuring materials are available to support daily operations.

The ideal candidate will have a practical, solutions-focused approach and enjoy working in a busy environment where accuracy, organisation and communication are essential.

Key Measures of Success
- Maintaining accurate stock records and inventory availability.
- Ensuring purchase orders are processed efficiently.
- Improving supplier delivery performance and resolving shortages.
- Reducing stock discrepancies, excess inventory and purchasing errors.
- Maintaining accurate SAP records and purchasing documentation.

Why Apply?
- Join an established organisation in a varied purchasing and stock control position.
- Take responsibility for important day-to-day purchasing and inventory activities.
- Work closely with suppliers and operational teams.
- Develop your experience using SAP and inventory management systems.
- Contribute to improving stock accuracy, purchasing processes and operational efficiency.

title: Logistics Co-Ordinator
description:
K.A.G. Recruitment is delighted to be working exclusively with our client, one of Europe's leading privately owned food processors, to recruit a Logistics Co-Ordinator for their operation in Oswestry.

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced logistics professional to play a key role in coordinating international exports, ensuring the efficient movement of goods, accurate documentation and successful delivery to customers.

Role: Logistics Co-Ordinator
Location: Oswestry, Shropshire
Salary: £35,000-£37,000 DOE
Hours: Monday-Friday, 40 hours per week (office-based flexibility on start/finish times due to business needs)

The Role
You will be responsible for coordinating transport, export administration and the movement of chilled goods through a third-party logistics provider, ensuring shipments are compliant, accurately documented and delivered on time.

Key Responsibilities:
- Consolidate site orders and commercial load manifests into timely load plans.
- Book approved carriers and coordinate goods receipt, checking, loading, despatch and delivery.
- Check physical goods against pre-advice, order details and supporting documentation.
- Ensure trailers are correctly temperature-set, securely loaded and sealed in line with procedures.
- Prepare and check export and import documentation, including health certificates, veterinary inspections and customs requirements.
- Monitor shipments through customs and sanitary inspections, resolving issues that could delay delivery.
- Investigate and record non-conformances, coordinating corrective actions with relevant stakeholders.
- Produce operational reports, check invoices and allocate or recharge transport costs to the appropriate sites.

Skills & Experience
You will be an organised and proactive individual with experience in FMCG transport or logistics administration, ideally within an international operation. You will have strong Excel skills, practical knowledge of export/import documentation and controls.

You'll also bring excellent attention to detail, resilience and strong communication, negotiation and relationship-building skills, with the ability to take ownership of issues and see them through to resolution.

Interested?
If you have the logistics experience and attention to detail needed to keep a busy export operation running smoothly, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply today to find out more about this opportunity through K.A.G. Recruitment.

The post holder will be working as part of a team along with other Medical and Clinical Administrators and Administrative Assistants. The post holder will be expected to be able to use their own initiative and judgement, although they will be well supported by other Mental Health Admin staff and through the clinical and professional networks accessible through the clinical teams. We are looking for someone that can identify with the following skills: Enthusiasm to provide a high-quality administrative service. Strong computer and keyboard skills in particular Word and Outlook. Attention to detail. Good grammar and written skills. Honesty, integrity and commitment. Quick thinking as priorities can change and flexibility to meet service need with a passion for quality. Strong and confident customer service skills. Team player. Able to work well in an ever-changing multi-professional team - including but not limited to Consultants, Prescribers and GP's. We are looking for a Medical and Clinical Administrator working 37.5 hours per week, supporting the CAMHS Mental Health Team based in Telford. Our Medical and Clinical Administrators are an integral part of our Admin Team,and our clinical teams rely on our team to provide an efficient, effective service to support them in delivering the very best care to our patients. The administration offices are busy, and the role is challenging but it is also rewarding. What will the role entail? Administration work including diary and clinic management for Consultant Psychiatrist/Doctors/Clinical Leads/Pathways and other Mental Health Professionals - scheduling appointments, supervisions etc. Type a range of documents including emailed requests, copy typing, and audio transcription. Use a variety of electronic systems (MS Office, RiO, E-Proc). Manage and deal with calls from families, carers, and other professionals. Confidently handling complex queries of a challenging/sensitive nature. Concise and accurate message taking. Using own initiative to proactively resolve problems. Minute taking. Day to Day operational tasks to support the Consultant Psychiatrist/Doctors/Clinical Leads and other Mental Health Professionals. Utilise the patient administration system (RiO) on a daily basis. Prioritise own workload and meet deadlines in order to meet the requirements of the post. For further information relating to this position please refer to the attached job description and specification.
